rock.why: Rock and terrain materials are pixel-for-pixel equivalent across A and B; the visible differences are in the liquid pools, which belong to another category.

lighting.why: The builds are nearly identical. B's faint back wall in the core chambers adds the midground/haze depth the brief asks for, which slightly outweighs its rectangle artifact and the flatter lava blocks.

identity.why: Palettes are effectively identical. B's caustic swirl and lit edges on the world-hued liquid make the pools, the main hue carrier at every depth, read slightly more as material, but the margin is marginal.

fluids.why: Nearly identical builds. A keeps the swirl and caustic texture on its fluid bodies. B flattens it and adds a hard rectangular lighter patch behind every core, which hurts the core chambers.

characters.why: B removes the red haze that flattened the dark around the glimmerflies and gives the shellback a readable shell. The other shots are nearly identical, so the margin is small.

vaults.why: Every A/B pair is visually identical apart from animation phase (bolt positions, lamp swing, rain); there is no difference in lighting, palette or readability.

ui.why: The UI is pixel-identical across hud-play, shop-trade, veil3-surface and ending-page. Title B is only marginally darker behind the tagline, which is not enough to separate the two.

minerals.why: The ore meshes, colours and glows look identical in every A/B pair; the only visible differences are on the pod, which is outside this category.
